summary: A 172-item checkpoint for reduction and Honda–Tate theory at the source allowed levels. It separates local B(G) inputs, global torus transfer, singular-base crystalline coefficients and Shimura CM lifting. Conditional general Hodge-type statements are distinguished from PEL A/C theorems and the disconnected type-D exercise. The author paper is fully read, but final-text reconciliation and recursive original-source closure remain open.

structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

qualifications: WittVector.isocrystal_classification assumes finrank exactly one; it does not supply Dieudonne-Manin in all ranks.
The reductive-group and torus predicates are built. Their rational Newton, sigma-conjugacy, local-global cohomology and Shimura interfaces are separate contracts.

The dominant-chamber uniqueness result is for a finite reduced crystallographic root system with the flipped pairing reduced and strictly ordered coefficients. The central torus and rational coroot cone adapters remain N05.
TauCeti.posRootCone in RootSystem/Positive.lean uses integral nonnegative coefficients. It does not by itself supply the rational dominance cone used here.
The abelian-variety and finite-surjective isogeny carriers are reused; the relative universal family, rational Hom tensor functor and isogeny torsors are additional contracts.
A divided-power structure is not a PD envelope, log site, convergent isocrystal or crystalline comparison theorem.
Proposed API wrappers on library items are not additional claims that their names or full contracts are implemented.

items.name: General rational-Levi minuscule lift (corrected: absolute Weyl group)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, M a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup, T⊂M a maximal torus, μ a minuscule cocharacter of M, and [b_M]∈B(M)_b such that ([b_M],{μ}) is G-admissible. Then there is w in the absolute Weyl group W(G,T)(Q̄_p), equivalently a G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T, such that ([b_M],{w·μ}) is M-admissible. The printed requirement w∈N_G(M)/M is false, by the GL₃ example with M=GL₁×GL₂, μ=(0,1,0), b_M=diag(p,1,1) (errata E2).
items.note: Corrected formulation and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026), following the structure of the paper's proof with the correct Weyl group. The only use, Corollary 1.1.17 (N32), needs exactly this: its proof writes "By Lemma 1.1.13, there exists w∈W(G,T)". The remaining inputs are N27 and its cited unramified result, and Kottwitz97 4.4, under G-local. The G-source gate for the normalizer statement is resolved by this correction.
proofSteps: Choose a rational parabolic P with Levi M and an inner twisting ξ:G→G* to the quasi-split form with ξ(P)=P* rational, as in the paper. Then ξ|_M:M→M* is an inner twisting, and B(M)_b≅π₁(M)_Γ=π₁(M*)_Γ≅B(M*)_b gives [b_{M*}].

Let μ* be the B*∩M*-dominant representative of ξ|_M∘μ. The pair ([b_{M*}],{μ*}) is G*-admissible. The κ-condition holds by functoriality of the Kottwitz maps and the compatible identifications π₁(M)=π₁(M*), π₁(G)=π₁(G*). The Newton condition holds because the Newton points of basic classes lie in X_*(A_{M*})_Q and are determined by κ ([Kot97, 4.4]). This is the paper's own argument.
Apply N27 (Proposition 1.1.13) to G*: there is w* in W(G*,T*), not only in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, with ([b_{M*}],{w*·μ*}) M*-admissible. The paper's proof misquotes this output as w*∈W(G*,M*).

Transport back along ξ, which identifies W(G,T)(Q̄_p) with W(G*,T*) after conjugating ξ(T) to T* inside M*. For basic b_M, M-admissibility of ([b_M],{μ′}) is the κ_M-equality κ_M(b_M)=μ′^♯ in π₁(M)_Γ (Lemma 1.1.6), which transports through π₁(M)=π₁(M*).

items.name: Rational abelian-quotient map
items.statement: There is a Q-group map I_x→G_ab whose base change equals the maps induced by i_ℓ for every ℓ. The auxiliary Shimura datum must be G′=G×_{G^ab}T, pairs (g,t) with the same image in G^ab, not the printed G×T.
items.note: Repair and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). With the printed G′=G×T the construction fails twice: G×T is not in GSp(V⊕V,ψ⊕ψ), and the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} contains 1×T, which maps onto G^ab. This is recorded in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22.json (E5). The remaining inputs, Corollary 2.1.9 and Noot, stay under G-noot.
proofSteps: For a special point (T,h_T) of (G,X) put G′=G×_{G^ab}T⊂G×T acting on V′=V⊕V, with T acting on the second copy through T⊂G. Similitude factors through G^ab, so G′⊂GSp(V′,ψ⊕ψ). Since h^ab is constant on X, X′=X×{h_T} maps into Hom(S,G′_R), giving an embedding of Shimura data (G′,X′)↪(GSp(V′),H′).

As in the paper, conjugating T→G by G^ad(Q), the point s₀ lifts to s′₀ on the integral model for (G′,X′). A_{s′₀} is isogenous to A_{s₀}×A_T, and I_{s′₀} preserves the decomposition. Restriction to A_T gives I_{s′₀}→T; compose with T→G^ab.

Kernel check: the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} (restriction to A_{s₀}) lies, after base change to any Q_ℓ, in ker(G′→G)={(1,t):t∈T∩G^der}. That kernel maps trivially to G^ab. So the composite kills ker(I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀}), and since I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} is surjective (Corollary 2.1.9) it factors through a Q-map I_{s₀}→G^ab.

Compatibility with i_ℓ: over Q_ℓ, the map I_{s₀}→G^ab so obtained and the composite I_{s₀}⊗Q_ℓ≅I_{ℓ,s₀}→G_{Q_ℓ}→G^ab_{Q_ℓ} agree on the image of I_{s′₀}, because for (g,t)∈G′ the images of g and t in G^ab coincide.

routes.brief: Build on Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties V4–V8), Shimura data (ShimuraData D3–D5), Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli M1–M4), Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli), AutomorphicBundles B1, finite-flat Dieudonne theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2), and PadicHodgeTheory R06.5. Import BunGAndNewtonStrata local theory, ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII global transfer, and CrystallineCohomologyConvergentPartII coefficient descent. Normalize the closure of the Hodge-type generic model at the lattice-stabilizer level. Construct lift-independent crystalline tensors, the family G-isocrystal and nonempty locally closed Newton strata for admissible classes satisfying (1.1.3.1); prove the lower Newton closure inclusion. State mu-ordinary nonemptiness with existence and rational-Newton witness, and density with local integrality. Prove the all-primes automorphism comparison, then independence of neat Weil conjugacy and rational maximal-torus transfer. For G quasi-split at p with no adjoint type-D factor, and explicitly assuming Conjecture 2.3.4 for all pairs, prove geometric coefficient-isogeny CM lifts for every point and every maximal torus of its isogeny group. Prove this unconditionally for PEL A/C. With G_der simply connected and ker1(Q,G_ab)=0 prove rational coefficient-isogeny CM lifts; specialize to C and A_n with n odd, retaining the separate odd-degree unitary argument. Preserve polarization similitudes, distinguish Qbar coefficient torsors from Q-points, and leave the disconnected type-D variant behind its exercise-proof gate. Do not generalize the motivic remarks to a proved abelian-type theorem.

Cover the proper semistable case first using the Eisenstein PD enlargement system, then the general case through alterations, proper descent and pointwise faithfulness. Keep horizontal and vertical log structures distinct. Import existing generic alterations/descent suppliers wherever exact contracts exist; specialize them here rather than re-planning their foundations.
